Redwood shows lower median latency on short context but tail spikes on 8k runs; throughput is competitive when batching is enabled. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-21 09:30 PT
Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Aurionix), Sofia (Aurionix), Daniel (Aurionix - CTO)

Summary note: audio was clear but a few names got garbled in auto-transcribe; timestamps every ~30s.

00:00 Jordan: ok hey everyone thanks for joining back for sprint pulse number three, um gonna kick off with a quick run through of the bench delta we shipped yesterday, Priya will walk the graphs and then we'll triage the tails.
00:18 Priya: yeah hi all, the slide I uploaded is in the deck link in chat, um key takeaways first; median token latency on 512-token prompts is about 120ms on Redwood vs 160ms on the incumbent, so p50 looks good, throughput in sustained mode with batching gives us about 220 rps on the 2-GPU slot for the model we tested.
00:40 Liam: quick q — is that batching set to 8 or 16? their config tends to use 8 in prod.
00:48 Priya: this run used batching=12 to smooth bursts; we have a parity run with 8, results are in the CSV but they were marginally lower throughput — 8 reduced latency slightly but lowered peak rps by ~12%.
01:05 Sofia: and what about 8k context? that's our bigger worry, we saw big tail latency spikes with the incumbent when queries hit long histories.
01:15 Priya: right so we ran three profiles: 512, 2k, and 8k. For 2k the p95 is 1.1s on Redwood vs 1.6s incumbent; for 8k median was 1.8s vs 2.0s, p95 on 8k however spiked to 6.8s in two runs on Redwood — we think that's KV-cache thrash under a near-random prompt mix.
01:40 Daniel: KV-cache thrash, can you explain that a little? our ops team saw similar with the baseline last month.
01:48 Priya: yeah so when you have many distinct conversational prefixes and clients with low prefix reuse, the KV cache can evict and reload frequently; that causes a jump in token prep/first-token latencies. We're seeing it particularly when sequence lengths vary a lot and batching interleaves requests.
02:12 Jordan: to be clear, baseline had a 9.2s p99 in their incident trace Liam shared earlier — our p99 peaks were lower but still present. we should do a head-to-head with identical prompt mix.
02:24 Liam: I uploaded the incident trace, sorry file name got munged by zoom.
02:30 Priya: got it. we also tried a config with per-client pinning (small cache partition) which reduced thrash but cost a little throughput. tradeoff, right.
02:45 Sofia: what was the unit token cost estimate on that config?
02:50 Jordan: in the spreadsheet we pushed, pinning raised effective per-token cost by about 6% because we could no longer share cache across high-traffic clients; I'll re-send a clarified sheet.
03:02 Liam: are there any latency SLO knobs? we have a 95th < 2.5s target for critical flows.
03:08 Priya: yes, two levers — aggressive routing to a lower-latency region or reserved dedicated slots with smaller batch sizes. Dedicated slots are predictable for p95 but cost more. We ran a dedicated-slot simulation: p95 dropped to ~1.4s on 8k scenarios but cost increased ~28%.
03:34 Jordan: note on routing — we can do a policy: if observed p95 over 10s window > threshold, route to fallback smaller model or dedicated pool. fallback content fidelity is slightly lower but keeps service live.
03:46 Daniel: fallback fidelity — do you have example regressions? we can't accept big hallucinations on the medical notes app.
03:52 Priya: understood. our fallback policy was constrained to a verified model variant; we ran evals and saw a 3-4% drop in exact-match on key extraction tasks, depends on prompt engineering. we can run your eval suite if you share it.
04:08 Liam: i'll get a representative prompt set up (— action).
04:12 Jordan: great. TL;DR on throughput: sustained throughput with caching and batching matches or exceeds incumbent in most mixes; short-context p50 is clearly better. tail behavior on long-context is resolvable with cache partitioning, pinning, or dedicated slots.
04:30 Sofia: ok can you run a 95th head-to-head with our exact prompts and our baseline provider? we need numbers we can show exec.
04:37 Jordan: yes we will. timeline?
04:39 Liam: asap, ideally by Monday.
04:41 Jordan: we can aim for Mon 2026-08-24, we'll need the prompt set and the baseline trace.
04:47 Liam: will send both today or tomorrow.
04:50 Priya: technical note — for the head-to-head we need to match: model weights, tokenizer versions, batch size, concurrency, and the same network egress characteristics. small mismatch in tokenizer can shift token counts and skew per-token cost.
05:06 Daniel: on security side last week we asked about audit logs and KMS; any updates there?
05:12 Jordan: yes, security docs were uploaded to the shared folder — SOC2 cert and KMS integration guide are in there, but for Private/VPC deployment we'll schedule a security review with your compliance folks.
05:23 Sofia: we will want HSM/KMS detail if we go private.
05:27 Jordan: noted.
05:30 Priya: also found an interesting perf pattern — when batching burstiness is high (lots of small requests) the scheduler queues cause micro-bimodal latency; smoothing at ingress with a small token holdback reduces p50 a bit but helps p95. Might be worth adding a small client-side jitter.
05:50 Liam: hmm that might be acceptable. we can add it to the client library.
05:55 Jordan: okay next, can we discuss the canary timeline? we proposed a 2-week pilot to start in production with 5% traffic to Redwood if the head-to-head looks good.
06:06 Daniel: our compliance needs a lifecycle doc but 5% seems feasible. Ops wants an automatic fallback to incumbent if p95 > 3s for 5 consecutive minutes.
06:17 Priya: we can wire that into routing; we already have a circuit-breaker that can pivot.
06:22 Sofia: show of hands — any blockers to running head-to-head?
06:25 Liam: only the prompt set and the baseline trace.
06:27 Jordan: we'll action the head-to-head and rerun routing with batching disabled to isolate KV-cache. Priya will attach logs.
06:35 Priya: i'll also test per-client pinning on a small shard and report throughput delta.
06:40 Jordan: great — recap of next steps: Redwood to run 95th head-to-head and share CSV, Priya to attach routing logs and pinning tests, Jordan to update pricing/throughput sheet, Aurionix to share prompt corpus and baseline trace, then schedule KV-cache deep-dive.
06:58 Sofia: thanks all, good sync.
07:02 Jordan: thanks — we'll follow up in email with calendar invite for the deep-dive.
07:06 End of meeting.
